_note: When each league page's football turned professional, and how its governing body treats the titles from before. 'since' is the first season counted as professional (amateur titles on the site are those of earlier years); 'treatment' is one of all (amateur titles count like the rest), pro-only (only professional titles count), none (no amateur national league: the championship started professional or later) or debated. Read by scripts/build_balance.py.

premier-league.milestone: Professionalism allowed by the FA in 1885; the Football League began in 1888
premier-league.note: The Football League was professional from its first season, so every title is a professional one.

la-liga.milestone: Professionalism allowed in 1926; La Liga began in 1929
la-liga.note: There was no national league before 1929, only regional championships and the Copa del Rey.

serie-a.milestone: The Carta di Viareggio allowed paid players in 1926; single-group Serie A since 1929–30
serie-a.note: The FIGC counts every scudetto since 1898, those of the amateur years included.

bundesliga.milestone: Paid contract players from 1948; the Bundesliga, the first nationwide professional league, in 1963
bundesliga.note: The DFB counts every German championship since 1903, before and since the Bundesliga.

ligue-1.note: The LFP counts titles only since 1932–33; the amateur championships (1894–1929) are shown on this site but are not in the official counts.

primeira-liga.milestone: The Campeonato da Liga in 1934–35; professional athletes recognized by law in 1960
primeira-liga.note: Every league title since 1934–35 counts; the earlier Campeonato de Portugal (1922–1938) counts as a cup, not a league title.

eredivisie.milestone: Professional football in 1954; the Eredivisie in 1956
eredivisie.note: The KNVB counts every Dutch title since 1888–89, those of the amateur final rounds included.

scottish-premiership.milestone: Professionalism allowed in 1893, the league's fourth season
scottish-premiership.note: The first three titles (1890–1893), won by amateurs, count like the rest.

super-lig.milestone: Professional football in 1951 (the Istanbul league); the national Süper Lig in 1959
super-lig.note: The TFF counts the Süper Lig (since 1959) and the Federation Cups of 1956–58, not the amateur national championships of 1924–1951; clubs have asked for those to be counted.

argentine-primera.milestone: The Liga Argentina de Football, professional, in 1931
argentine-primera.note: The AFA counts every title since 1891: amateur, professional and those of the rival associations of the split years.

brasileirao.milestone: Professionalism in the state leagues in 1933; the national championship from 1959
brasileirao.note: The national championship began in 1959 (the 1937 tournament was recognized in 2023), so there are no amateur national titles; amateur football was played in the state championships.

uruguayan-primera.note: The AUF counts every title since 1900, amateur and professional.

paraguayan-primera.note: The APF counts every title since 1906, amateur and professional.

chilean-primera.note: The national league was born professional; earlier football was played in regional associations.

colombian-primera.note: There was no national championship before the professional league.

ecuadorian-serie-a.milestone: Professional football in Guayaquil from 1951; the national championship in 1957
ecuadorian-serie-a.note: The national championship began professional in 1957; earlier titles were provincial.

peruvian-primera.note: The FPF counts every title since 1912, amateur and professional.

bolivian-primera.milestone: Professional football from 1950; the Liga del Fútbol Profesional from 1977
bolivian-primera.note: Most lists count titles since 1950, when football turned professional; others start with the professional league of 1977, so club totals differ.

liga-mx.note: Liga MX counts titles from 1943–44; the amateur championships (1902–1943) are not counted.

mls.note: MLS was a professional league from the start.
